To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the developing brain is highly susceptible to essential fatty acid (EFA) deficiency.
the brain of the developing rat is highly susceptible to essential fatty acid (EFA) deficiency.

EFA deficiency is produced not by feeding fat free diet but a diet high in unsaturated but low in polyunsaturated acids and that the deficiency in the brain is manifested by an increase in triene/tetrene ratios, a decrease in lipid/ protein ratio and an unusually low amount in odd chain fatty acid in EPG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of essential fatty acid deficiency on the developing brain.
the effects of dietary fat on the developing nervous system.
the effect of EFA deficiency on brain development and its effect on the lipid metabolism of brain subcellular components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EFA deficiency in the developing brain is produced by the competition of oleic acid in the utilization of dietary linoleic acid.
the brain of the rat, like other organs and tissues, requires essential fatty acids for normal development and growth.
the brain of the rat is very sensitive to the EFA deficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EFA is essential for the developing brain and that it is required in the early stage of brain development.
EFA deficiency in the rat brain is not a simple phenomenon and is not produced by a simple diet devoid of essential fatty acids.

the developing brain has a high capacity to synthesize fatty acids and the EFA deficiency state is not the result of an impaired ability to synthesize fatty acid, but the result of competition from oleic for linoleic acid in the synthesis of fatty acid in the developing brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EFA deficiency can be produced in the developing brain by feeding a diet which contains high amounts of oleic acid.
the brain is not a self-contained organ and its development is influenced by the diet of the mother.
the competition from oleic but not from saturated fatty acids in the diet results in the deficiency state.
